newsitem.title: USA: Optical Sensors to relaunch SensiCath.
newsitem.headline: Optical Sensors to relaunch SensiCath.

text.p: Optical Sensors Inc said Wednesday it had sufficient financial resources to fund an anticipated relaunch of its SensiCath Sensor later in this year after a voluntary recall in May.

"Our financial condition remains strong," Sam Humphries, president and chief executive, said in a statement. "At the end of the second quarter we had $23.5 million in cash, and our financial resources remain sufficient to support an anticipated relaunch of the SensiCath Sensor later in the current calendar year."
Earlier, Optical Sensors said it lost $3.2 million, or $0.39 a share, in the second quarter compared with a loss of $2.6 million, or $0.31 a share, in the same period last year.

Results were hurt by the company's voluntary recall of SensiCath Sensors that were in customers' inventories. The product, which monitors the blood of ill babies, was not accurately recording acidity in cases where children had high levels of bilirubin, said Paulita LaPlante, vice president.
All SensiCath sensors were retrieved from customers, the company said.

"Since voluntarily initiating the retrieval of the SensiCath Sensor, we have been working to develop a modification to the pH sensor which overcomes the measurement interference that we identified," Humphries said.

"We have developed a modification to the pH sensor which provides accurate pH readings despite clinically significant bilirubin levels," he said. "The modification is producing the desired measurement accuracy under laboratory conditions, and we are currently testing and evaluating the requisite modification to our manufacturing process for the pH sensor. The next steps will be to validate the manufacturing process and resume patient-attached evaluations at key customer sites."
